about: Steelbound Brewery & Distillery opened in May 2018 in Ellicottville, the ski town in the hills south of Buffalo, at the corner of Routes 219 and 242. It calls itself one of New York’s first places to put a brewery, a distillery, a bar and a restaurant under one roof. Co-owner Bill Bursee has since added locations in Springville and Dunkirk. The Buffalo Bills-themed taproom pours dozens of house beers alongside spirits made on site.

Steelbound’s agave spirits are an unusual hybrid that the distillery calls a New York-style tequila. The recipe is 75 percent New York corn and 25 percent Mexican blue agave, made by a process Steelbound says it spent more than a year developing. Because it is made in New York and is not all agave, it cannot legally be called tequila; it is sold as an agave spirit. The Blanco is the unaged version, bottled clear.

Steelbound launched its tequilas at its five-year anniversary party around Cinco de Mayo 2023, alongside a set of new bourbons, and its Reposado is the same spirit rested in oak. In the glass, expect the bright, vegetal agave notes of a young blanco carried on a softer, slightly sweet corn base. It works in a Margarita or a Paloma, the way a blanco tequila would.
